clue.text: Element in force?

definitions.meaning: British slang for a police officer, someone serving in the police force

explanation.surface: A riddle asking which element is at work within some force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In force' reads as a physics term, but it means serving in the police force; a copper is a British police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is both a reddish metallic element and everyday British slang for a police constable.

clue.text: Something Mexican stored in university vaults

indicators.note: stored in says the Mexican food is kept within the university abbreviation

parts.note: Camb is short for Cambridge University
a taco is a Mexican folded tortilla

explanation.surface: Mexican food kept in college cellars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vaults' look like a verb or bank strongrooms but are underground burial chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: Catacombs are underground burial tunnels or chambers.

clue.text: Yellow, dull material round the border

indicators.note: round says the dull writing goes around the edge word

parts.note: prose is plain, unpoetic writing
a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: Drab yellow cloth with an edging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' suggests fabric, but here it means written material; 'round' wraps the dull writing about the edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Primrose is a pale yellow, the colour of the spring flower.

clue.text: Around start of lunchtime, cook a rice cake

indicators.note: around says the cooked letters go about the opening of lunchtime
cook says the letters of a rice are worked into a new form
start of means just the first letter of lunchtime is taken

explanation.surface: At lunchtime, cook a rice cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' turns A RICE into ECAIR, and 'Around' puts it about L from 'start of lunchtime'.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a finger-shaped choux pastry filled with cream.

clue.text: These days herb contains speed

indicators.note: contains says the herb holds the next word within it

parts.note: sage is a kitchen herb
pace means speed

explanation.surface: Nowadays a herb comes laced with amphetamine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speed' looks like the drug, but it simply means rate of movement; 'contains' puts it inside the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: The space age is a name for the modern era of rockets and satellites, the present time.

clue.text: Fat, short, posh voice

indicators.note: short means the word for fat loses its final letter

parts.note: plump means fat

explanation.surface: A stout, short person who talks posh.
explanation.walkthrough: A plummy voice, said as with a plum in the mouth, is a British marker of upper-class speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Plum describes a rich, upper-class voice, as in speaking with a plum in one's mouth.

clue.text: Something refined appears good in weapon

indicators.note: in says the letter for good goes within the weapon

parts.note: a cutlass is a short sailor's sword

explanation.surface: Something classy turns out good in battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Cut glass also means a refined British accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut glass is fine decorated crystal, and the term also means a posh, refined accent.

clue.text: Come to a watercourse, end first

indicators.note: end first means the last letter of the stream word moves to its front

parts.note: a river is a watercourse

explanation.surface: Reach a stream, where the river ends first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End first' moves the watercourse's final R to its front, giving RRIVE, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrive is to come to a place.

clue.text: Old drink to ship out

parts.note: ex means former, old
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Old wine to send overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ship out' looks like a sailor's departure but means send abroad for sale.
explanation.definitionFit: To export goods is to send them abroad for sale.

clue.text: Very small amount of pudding

definitions.meaning: a ... is a tiny quantity, as in 'a ... tired'
a layered British dessert of sponge, fruit, custard and cream

explanation.walkthrough: A trifle is a classic British pudding (dessert) of sponge, jelly, custard and cream.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a negligible quantity and a layered custard-and-sponge dessert.

clue.text: Flatter, say, for investment in local backing

indicators.note: investment in means one word is clothed within the other
backing means the word for a local is read from right to left

parts.note: a local is a British term for one's neighbourhood pub
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: Praise someone, perhaps, to get funding for the neighbourhood's support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' turns the pub word into BUP, and 'investment in' places the speaking word inside it, after the B. A 'local' is British slang for one's nearby pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To butter someone up is to flatter or soft-soap them to win favour.

clue.text: Isn't into cunning, being virtuous

indicators.note: into says the contraction goes inside the word for cunning

parts.note: sly means cunning
ain't is a colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: Not being cunning means being good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into' puts the slangy contraction inside the cunning word; 'being' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Saintly means pious, righteous, good like a holy person.

clue.text: Couple of couples getting stuffed in sexy party

indicators.note: getting stuffed in says the pairs are packed inside the next word

parts.note: carnal means sexual, sensual
two pairs make four, IV in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Two pairs of lovers join a racy party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couple of couples' suggests swingers but is just four in Roman numerals; 'getting stuffed in' packs it inside the sexy word.
explanation.definitionFit: A carnival is a festive public celebration, a big street party.

clue.text: Bird fancier after pigeon, primarily

indicators.note: after says the next word follows that opening letter
primarily means only the opening letter of pigeon is used

parts.note: a fancier, someone keen on something, is a lover of it

explanation.surface: A bird-fancier is mainly interested in pigeons.
explanation.walkthrough: Pigeon fanciers are a real hobby, so 'fancier' looks tied to 'pigeon'; here it is LOVER, placed after P.
explanation.definitionFit: The plover is a wading bird of shores and fields.

clue.text: Wrap right from neck to toe, if this is cold?.

definitions.text: Wrap right from neck to toe, if this is cold?.

parts.words: Wrap right from neck to toe, if this is cold?.
parts.note: advice to bundle up head to foot when conditions outside are chilly

explanation.surface: Advice to dress warmly from head to foot when it is chilly.
explanation.definitionFit: When the climate outside turns cold, people wrap up warmly.

clue.text: Film not seen, but heard

indicators.note: heard says the word for 'not seen' is taken by its sound

parts.note: something not seen has been missed

explanation.surface: A movie nobody watched, though people heard it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' suggests a movie, but it is a thin layer, as in a film of mist.
explanation.definitionFit: A mist is a fine haze of droplets, a thin film over glass or air.

clue.text: Anger at smoke

definitions.meaning: the fragrant smoke of burning resin or sticks

explanation.surface: Fury at someone lighting up.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means enrage; as a noun it is perfumed smoke from burning spices.

clue.text: One pulling out all the stops given unlikely roasting

definitions.text: One pulling out all the stops

indicators.note: unlikely means the letters of the word are scrambled into an improbable order

explanation.surface: Someone going all out after a harsh scolding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulling out all the stops' sounds like maximum effort, but organ stops are literally pulled out to sound.
explanation.definitionFit: An organist pulls the stops on a pipe organ to choose its voices.

clue.text: Camp in a forest, only partial cover

indicators.note: only partial says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Camping in woods gives only partial shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinafore is an apron or dress worn over clothes to protect them.

clue.text: Spinner given bouncer becomes unbalanced

parts.note: a top is a spinning toy
a heavy is a burly bouncer or minder

explanation.surface: A bowler delivering a bouncer becomes erratic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinner' and 'bouncer' suggest cricket deliveries but are a toy top and a doorman, a heavy.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-heavy means having too much weight at the top, so unstable.

clue.text: Clergyman on time?

definitions.meaning: a bishop or other senior churchman
read as ..., before being late, so punctual

explanation.surface: Asking whether the vicar is punctual.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as pre-late: before late, so on time.
explanation.definitionFit: A prelate is a high-ranking member of the clergy such as a bishop.

clue.text: Alcoholic to lose everything?

definitions.meaning: a drunk who favours cheap wine
read as ..., to win nothing, O being zero

explanation.surface: Does a drinker always end up losing it all?
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as WIN O: to win nothing at all is to lose everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A wino is a habitual drunkard, especially one who drinks cheap wine.

clue.text: Judge smoke rising to be the boss

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the words are read from bottom to top

parts.note: ref is short for referee, a judge
fag is British slang for a cigarette

explanation.surface: A judge whose cigarette smoke rises becomes the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' reverses REF + FAG to GAF + FER. GAFFER is British for the boss, FAG for a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaffer is British informal for a foreman or manager.

clue.text: Small bump suddenly came up

parts.note: a prang is British slang for a minor car crash

explanation.surface: A small collision suddenly cropped up.
explanation.walkthrough: PRANG is British slang for a minor car accident.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprang is the past tense of spring, to leap up or appear suddenly.

clue.text: Pet to feed swallowing last of dinner

indicators.note: swallowing says the word for feed takes in a letter

parts.note: to stoke is to feed a fire or furnace

indicators.note: last of means only the final letter of dinner is used

explanation.surface: Feeding a pet after it eats the remains of dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' looks like an animal but is a verb, to stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: To pet an animal is to stroke or caress it.

clue.text: A strip said to sound inviting

indicators.note: said means the phrase 'a strip' is taken as it is spoken

parts.note: a peel is a strip of skin or rind, as in a peel of orange

explanation.surface: A striptease described as alluring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A strip' hints at undressing but is A PEEL, a piece of rind.
explanation.definitionFit: To appeal is to be attractive or tempting, to seem inviting.

clue.text: Heart has broken, given result of overexposure

indicators.note: broken means the letters of the two words are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A heartbroken lover after too much exposure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' rearranges HEARTHAS; 'overexposure' means too much sun, not emotional openness.
explanation.definitionFit: Prickly heat, a skin rash, follows too much heat and sun.

clue.text: Twelve and rising

indicators.note: rising in a down clue says the word reads the same from the bottom upwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Midday, and climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the word reads the same upwards as down.
explanation.definitionFit: Noon is midday, twelve o'clock.

clue.text: One would do the pressing when inexperienced person embraced by tart

indicators.note: embraced by says the novice is held inside the pastry word

parts.note: a flan is an open tart
a tiro is a beginner or novice

explanation.surface: A novice cuddled by a floozy would do the ironing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' suggests a person but is a FLAN, holding TIRO. The definition is a flatiron, an old iron heated on a stove.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatiron is an iron for smoothing clothes, heated on a fire before electric irons.

clue.text: Where millions of South Americans got constricted by appropriate beast?

indicators.note: constricted by says the word got is squeezed inside the snake

parts.note: a boa is a constrictor, the fitting animal for something constricted

explanation.surface: Many South Americans were squeezed by a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' because a boa constrictor squeezes its prey.
explanation.definitionFit: Bogota, Colombia's capital, is home to millions of people.

clue.text: Pasta — fix a lot for one

parts.note: to rig is to fix dishonestly
a ton is informal for a lot
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Fix a lot of pasta for one person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' only links the pieces; 'a lot' looks like one phrase but gives A and TON.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigatoni is a ridged tube-shaped pasta.

clue.text: Let me introduce an unknown belief in the unorthodox

parts.note: here's is the phrase for presenting someone
Y is a mathematical unknown, like x

explanation.surface: Presenting an unknown: an unorthodox belief.
explanation.walkthrough: Algebra uses x, y and z as unknowns.
explanation.definitionFit: Heresy is a belief contrary to orthodox doctrine.
